Bug_Title: MC: An overridable method is called from the clone() method. (MC_OVERRIDABLE_METHOD_CALL_IN_CLONE)
Bug_Details:
Calling overridable methods from the clone() method is insecure because a subclass could override the method,
affecting the behavior of clone(). It can also observe or modify the clone object in a partially initialized
state. Only static, final or private methods should be invoked from the clone() method. 
See SEI CERT rule
MET06-J. Do not invoke overridable methods in clone().
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the clone() method where an overridable method setValue() is being called. This can lead to unpredictable behavior as a subclass could override the setValue() method, affecting the behavior of clone().
Trigger_Explanation: The testCloneMethod triggers the bug by calling the showBug method which in turn calls the clone method. The clone method, as implemented in the BuggyClone class, contains a call to an overridable method (setValue) which leads to unpredictable behavior.
